candidates.statement: Gateway checkout POSTs return 502 because the downstream order service returns 500 on POST /v1/orders; traces and logs show each checkout 502 paired with an order 500 within milliseconds, so the gateway is propagating an order-service server error.
candidates.uncertainty: Order-service internal cause (db, payment, inventory) not observed; only gateway-side evidence available.

report.explanation: Checkout 502s are fast (15-63ms) and consistently paired with order-service 500s in traces and logs, indicating the gateway relays an order-service server error rather than a gateway-local fault. Order-service internals are unobserved, so the specific downstream cause is not established.
missing_evidence: Order-service traces/logs for POST /v1/orders to identify the internal 500 cause
Order-service dependency metrics (postgresql, payment, inventory) to rule out db-pool-exhaustion or downstream-latency
